questions.question: What is the main role of a catalyst in a chemical reaction?
options: It slows down a reaction to make it safer.
It speeds up a reaction and is completely used up.
It speeds up a reaction without being used up or chemically changed.
It reacts with the products to turn them back into reactants.

questions.question: Which statement is true about how catalysts work with different chemical reactions?
options: The same catalyst can speed up every known chemical reaction.
Catalysts are specific, meaning different reactions require different catalysts.
Catalysts only work for reactions involving metals and acids.
Any catalyst can be used as long as the temperature is high enough.

questions.question: What are enzymes?
options: Biological catalysts that speed up reactions in living cells.
Synthetic chemicals used to clean up oil spills in oceans.
Tiny minerals that strengthen the walls of plant cells.
Non-living chemical compounds that slow down digestion.

questions.question: What happens when a more reactive metal is added to a solution of a less reactive metal's salt?
options: The less reactive metal is destroyed and turns into gas.
No reaction occurs because salts are always stable.
The more reactive metal will displace the less reactive metal from its salt.
Both metals dissolve completely to form a new alloy.

questions.question: When magnesium is added to copper sulfate solution, what are the products of this displacement reaction?
options: Magnesium sulfate solution and copper
Copper sulfate solution and magnesium oxide
Magnesium hydroxide and copper oxide
Copper hydride and magnesium sulfate.

questions.question: How can displacement reactions be useful in studying metals?
options: They can be used to turn any cheap metal into gold.
They can confirm the position of a metal in the reactivity series.
They measure the exact melting point of a metal.
They show how easily a metal conducts electricity.

questions.question: What is a metal ore?
options: A pure block of metal found deep underground.
A mixture of gases from which metals are condensed.
A type of rock that contains a metal in a form that can be extracted.
A synthetic alloy created in a laboratory.

questions.question: Under what condition can carbon be used to extract a metal from its ore?
options: Carbon can only extract metals that are more reactive than carbon.
Carbon can extract some metals when carbon is more reactive than the metal.
Carbon must be less reactive than the metal for extraction to work.
Carbon can only be used if the metal is liquid at room temperature.

questions.question: Which of the following is a typical set of physical properties for metals?
options: Brittle, dull, poor thermal conductors, and low density.
Good conductors of heat and electricity, strong, shiny, malleable, and ductile.
Soft, easy to melt, transparent, and highly flexible.
Liquid at room temperature, highly acidic, and chemically unreactive.

questions.question: How are ceramics made, and how do their properties change during the process?
options: They are made from hard gases that soften when they are cooled.
They are made from soft substances and become hard and brittle when heated.
They are made from melted metals that become flexible when cooled in water.
They are made from liquid polymers that remain soft forever.

questions.question: What are plastics made of, and do they all behave the same way?
options: Plastics are made of pure metals, and they all have identical properties.
Plastics are made of silica, and they all melt at the same temperature.
Plastics are made from polymers, and there are many types with very different properties.
Plastics are made from natural sugars, and they are all biodegradable.

questions.question: What is an alloy?
options: A compound made entirely of non-metals.
A pure element that has been highly polished.
A mixture of elements that includes at least one metal.
A plastic that has been reinforced with glass fibers.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of creating a composite material?
options: To combine different materials to create a new material with improved properties.
To break down a complex mixture into its pure elements.
To make a material cheaper by adding useless filler.
To turn a solid material into a liquid for easier transport.

questions.question: How are polymers structured at the molecular level?
options: They consist of individual metal atoms arranged in a giant lattice.
They are made from small molecules called monomers joined to form very long chains.
They are made of isolated water molecules that do not touch each other.
They are composed of short, disconnected rings of carbon atoms.

questions.question: Why do some polymers have high melting points?
options: Because they are made entirely of metal atoms.
Because their molecules are very small and can move easily.
Because their long polymer molecules are hard to separate.
Because they contain trapped pockets of high-pressure gas.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the origin of polymers?
options: All polymers must be manufactured synthetically in factories.
Polymers can only be found in nature and cannot be made synthetically.
Polymers can be made synthetically, but some also exist naturally.
Polymers only form when volcanic lava cools rapidly.

questions.question: What is the effect of adding a plasticiser to a polymer?
options: It makes the polymer extremely brittle and easy to shatter.
It gets between polymer molecules, allowing them to move over each other more easily.
It causes the polymer to instantly dissolve in cold water.
It locks the polymer chains tightly together so they cannot move at all.

questions.question: What happens to a polymer's properties when cross-links form between its molecules?
options: The polymer becomes harder and less flexible.
The polymer becomes a liquid at room temperature.
The polymer becomes much softer and easier to stretch.
The polymer loses its ability to conduct heat.

questions.question: When certain metals react with an acid, what products are formed?
options: A metal hydroxide and carbon dioxide gas
A metal oxide and oxygen gas
A metal salt and hydrogen gas
Pure carbon and water vapor.

questions.question: What are the products when a reactive metal reacts with water?
options: A metal oxide and nitrogen gas
A metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas
A metal chloride and oxygen gas
A metal carbonate and steam.
